name: Wenyang Jia
about: This journal is closer to an unfinished film: still being shot, still changing locations, and probably never meant to end with a clean final scene.

The journey has covered many kinds of signals: near-infrared spectra, hyperspectral images, REIMS and MALDI-ToF mass fingerprints, LC–MS/MS data, sensory responses, peptide sequences, chemometric models, and software pipelines. It has also passed through different kinds of questions: What makes food authentic? How can quality be measured before it is too late? Can a spectrum, a peptide, or a mass-spectrometry fingerprint tell a better story than the eye can see? What would the future look like when AI encounters biology?
Some scenes became papers. Some became software. Some became databases, unfinished tools, conference talks, patents, field trials, and ideas still waiting for the right form.
interests: AI-enabled design for proteins, peptides, and microbial hosts
Interpretable machine learning and chemometrics for omics data matrices
Functional peptide discovery and high-throughput analytical automation
Spectroscopy and mass spectrometry linked to authenticity, quality, and product sense-making
